facts.statement: The type specimen of Bicharracosaurus was discovered in Chubut Province, Argentina, near the Chubut River.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Bicharracosaurus dionidei, MPEF-PV 1730, was discovered in Chubut Province, Argentina, in the central part of the outcrop area near the Chubut River.

facts.statement: The fossil was reported by local farmer Dionide Mesa in March 2001.
facts.quote: It was reported by a local farmer, Dionide Mesa, in March 2001.

facts.statement: The generic name Bicharracosaurus combines the Spanish word for 'big animal' and the Greek word for 'lizard'.
facts.quote: The generic name, Bicharracosaurus, combines the informal Spanish word bicharraco, meaning 'big animal'—in reference to its huge size—and the Latinised Greek word saurus, meaning 'lizard'.

facts.statement: The specific name dionidei honors the farmer Dionide Mesa who discovered the specimen.
facts.quote: The specific name, dionidei, is after the farmer Dionide Mesa who found this specimen.

facts.statement: Bicharracosaurus had an estimated length of 15 meters and a weight of 20 tonnes.
facts.quote: Bicharracosaurus had an estimated length of 15 m and a weight of 20 t.

facts.statement: The middle and rear tail vertebrae feature a triangular pneumatic hole in the centrodiapophyseal fossa.
facts.quote: In the middle and rear tail vertebrae, the centrodiapophyseal fossa is pierced by a triangular pneumatic hole.

facts.statement: The rearmost neck vertebrae have a small upward-pointing protuberance at the lower end of the postzygodiapophyseal lamina.
facts.quote: With the rearmost neck vertebrae, the postzygodiapophyseal lamina at its lower end has a small upwardly directed protuberance.

facts.statement: The sacral vertebrae possess boat-shaped joint facets on their centra.
facts.quote: The centra of the sacral vertebrae have boat-shaped joint facets.

facts.statement: Bicharracosaurus is classified as a macronarian sauropod, possibly related to brachiosaurids.
facts.quote: Bicharracosaurus () is a genus of macronarian sauropod dinosaur, possibly a brachiosaurid, known from the Late Jurassic Cañadón Calcáreo Formation of Argentina.

facts.statement: Bicharracosaurus belongs to the unranked family Macronaria.
Bicharracosaurus lived during the Late Jurassic, specifically the Oxfordian to Kimmeridgian stages.
Bicharracosaurus lived between 161.5 and 149.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Kimmeridgian (161.5 to 149.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils of Bicharracosaurus are known from the Cañadón Calcáreo Formation in Argentina.
facts.quote: known from the Late Jurassic Cañadón Calcáreo Formation of Argentina.

facts.statement: The phylogenetic position of Bicharracosaurus has been tested using datasets containing basal eusauropods and neosauropods.
It is debated whether Bicharracosaurus is closely related to Tehuelchesaurus benitezii, as phylogenetic analyses yield inconsistent results regarding their relationship.
The early evolution of macronarians is hindered by incongruent phylogenetic positions of related taxa depending on the dataset used.

rejected.statement: Alexandra Reutter and colleagues described Bicharracosaurus dionidei as a new genus and species in 2026.
rejected.quote: In 2026, Alexandra Reutter and colleagues described Bicharracosaurus dionidei as a new genus and species of macronarian sauropod based on these fossil remains.
